text.p: The Mexican energy ministry Tuesday released financial details of the state-owned petrochemical plants in which it is aiming to sell a 49 percent stake to private and foreign investors.
"As of July 31, the general balance of Pemex Petrochemicals shows total assets of 25.498 billion pesos, while the value of fixed assets is 18.029 billion pesos," the ministry said in a statement.
"The accounts of the Pemex subsidiary show total liabilities of 8.159 billion pesos."
It said liabilities included 2.071 billion pesos in short-term debt and 3.965 billion pesos in long-term debt.

The government had originally planned to sell off 100 percent of the unit of state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) but recently revised the plan in the face of fierce political opposition to a full sale.
The sell-off involves 61 petrochemical plants in state hands.
